2517 !-------------------------!
2518 ! Buoyancy-Sorting Mixing !
2519 !-------------------------!------------------------------------------------ !
2520 ! !
2521 ! In order to complete buoyancy-sorting mixing at layer mid-point, and so !
2522 ! calculate 'updraft mass flux, updraft w velocity, conservative scalars' !
2523 ! at the upper interface of each layer, we need following 3 information. !
2524 ! !
2525 ! 1. Pressure where mixing occurs ('pe'), and temperature at 'pe' which is !
2526 ! necessary to calculate various thermodynamic coefficients at pe. This !
2527 ! temperature is obtained by undiluted cumulus properties lifted to pe. !
2528 ! 2. Undiluted updraft properties at pe - conservative scalar and vertical !
2529 ! velocity -which are assumed to be the same as the properties at lower !
2530 ! interface only for calculation of fractional lateral entrainment and !
2531 ! detrainment rate ( fer(k) and fdr(k) [Pa-1] ), respectively. Final !
2532 ! values of cumulus conservative scalars and w at the top interface are !
2533 ! calculated afterward after obtaining fer(k) & fdr(k). !
2534 ! 3. Environmental properties at pe. !
2535 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
2536
2537 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
2538 ! Define cumulus scale height. !
2539 ! Cumulus scale height is defined as the maximum height cumulus can reach. !
2540 ! In case of premitive code, cumulus scale height ('cush') at the current !
2541 ! time step was assumed to be the same as 'cush' of previous time step. !
2542 ! However, I directly calculated cush at each time step using an iterative !
2543 ! method. Note that within the cumulus scheme, 'cush' information is used !
2544 ! only at two places during buoyancy-sorting process: !
2545 ! (1) Even negatively buoyancy mixtures with strong vertical velocity !
2546 ! enough to rise up to 'rle*scaleh' (rle = 0.1) from pe are entrained !
2547 ! into cumulus updraft, !
2548 ! (2) The amount of mass that is involved in buoyancy-sorting mixing !
2549 ! process at pe is rei(k) = rkm/scaleh/rho*g [Pa-1] !
2550 ! In terms of (1), I think critical stopping distance might be replaced by !
2551 ! layer thickness. In future, we will use rei(k) = (0.5*rkm/z0(k)/rho/g). !
2552 ! In the premitive code, 'scaleh' was largely responsible for the jumping !
2553 ! variation of precipitation amount. !
2554 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
2555
2556635893635893 scaleh = tscaleh
25576331563315 if( tscaleh .lt. 0.0_r8 ) scaleh = 1000._r8
2558
2559 ! Save time : Set iter_scaleh = 1. This will automatically use 'cush' from the previous time step
2560 ! at the first implicit iteration. At the second implicit iteration, it will use
2561 ! the updated 'cush' by the first implicit cin. So, this updating has an effect of
2562 ! doing one iteration for cush calculation, which is good.
2563 ! So, only this setting of 'iter_scaleh = 1' is sufficient-enough to save computation time.
2564 ! OK
2565
256619076792543572 do iter_scaleh = 1, 3
2567
2568 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------- !
2569 ! Initialization of 'kbup' and 'kpen' !
2570 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------- !
2571 ! 'kbup' is the top-most layer in which cloud buoyancy is positive !
2572 ! both at the top and bottom interface of the layer. 'kpen' is the !
2573 ! layer upto which cumulus panetrates ,i.e., cumulus w at the base !
2574 ! interface is positive, but becomes negative at the top interface.!
2575 ! Here, we initialize 'kbup' and 'kpen'. These initializations are !
2576 ! not trivial but important, expecially in calculating turbulent !
2577 ! fluxes without confliction among several physics as explained in !
2578 ! detail in the part of turbulent fluxes calculation later. Note !
2579 ! that regardless of whether 'kbup' and 'kpen' are updated or not !
2580 ! during updraft motion, penetrative entrainments are dumped down !
2581 ! across the top interface of 'kbup' later. More specifically,!
2582 ! penetrative entrainment heat and moisture fluxes are calculated !
2583 ! from the top interface of 'kbup' layer to the base interface of !
2584 ! 'kpen' layer. Because of this, initialization of 'kbup' & 'kpen' !
2585 ! influence the convection system when there are not updated. The !
2586 ! below initialization of 'kbup = krel' assures that penetrative !
2587 ! entrainment fluxes always occur at interfaces above the PBL top !
2588 ! interfaces (i.e., only at interfaces k >=kinv ), which seems to !
2589 ! be attractable considering that the most correct fluxes at the !
2590 ! PBL top interface can be ontained from the 'fluxbelowinv' using !
2591 ! reconstructed PBL height. !
2592 ! The 'kbup = krel'(after going through the whole buoyancy sorting !
2593 ! proces during updraft motion) implies that cumulus updraft from !
2594 ! the PBL top interface can not reach to the LFC,so that 'kbup' is !
2595 ! not updated during upward. This means that cumulus updraft did !
2596 ! not fully overcome the buoyancy barrier above just the PBL top. !
2597 ! If 'kpen' is not updated either ( i.e., cumulus cannot rise over !
2598 ! the top interface of release layer),penetrative entrainment will !
2599 ! not happen at any interfaces. If cumulus updraft can rise above !
2600 ! the release layer but cannot fully overcome the buoyancy barrier !
2601 ! just above PBL top interface, penetratve entrainment occurs at !
2602 ! several above interfaces, including the top interface of release !
2603 ! layer. In the latter case, warming and drying tendencies will be !
2604 ! be initiated in 'krel' layer. Note current choice of 'kbup=krel' !
2605 ! is completely compatible with other flux physics without double !
2606 ! or miss counting turbulent fluxes at any interface. However, the !
2607 ! alternative choice of 'kbup=krel-1' also has itw own advantage - !
2608 ! when cumulus updraft cannot overcome buoyancy barrier just above !
2609 ! PBL top, entrainment warming and drying are concentrated in the !
2610 ! 'kinv-1' layer instead of 'kinv' layer for this case. This might !
2611 ! seems to be more dynamically reasonable, but I will choose the !
2612 ! 'kbup = krel' choice since it is more compatible with the other !
2613 ! parts of the code, expecially, when we chose ' use_emf=.false. ' !
2614 ! as explained in detail in turbulent flux calculation part. !
2615 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------- !
2616
261719076791907679 kbup = krel
2618 kpen = krel
2619
2620 ! ------------------------------------------------------------ !
2621 ! Since 'wtw' is continuously updated during vertical motion, !
2622 ! I need below initialization command within this 'iter_scaleh'!
2623 ! do loop. Similarily, I need initializations of environmental !
2624 ! properties at 'krel' layer as below. !
2625 ! ------------------------------------------------------------ !
2626
2627 wtw = wlcl * wlcl
2628 pe = 0.5_r8 * ( prel + ps0(krel) )
2629 dpe = prel - ps0(krel)
263019076793815358 exne = exnf(pe)
2631 thvebot = thv0rel
2632 thle = thl0(krel) + ssthl0(krel) * ( pe - p0(krel) )
2633 qte = qt0(krel) + ssqt0(krel) * ( pe - p0(krel) )
2634 ue = u0(krel) + ssu0(krel) * ( pe - p0(krel) )
2635 ve = v0(krel) + ssv0(krel) * ( pe - p0(krel) )
2636108737703108737703 do m = 1, ncnst
2637 tre(m) = tr0(krel,m) + sstr0(krel,m) * ( pe - p0(krel) )
2638 enddo
2639
2640 !*************
2641 !Water tracers
2642 !*************
264319076791907679 if(trace_water) then
264476307169538395 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
2645 wte(m) = wt0(krel,m) + sswt0(krel,m) * ( pe - p0(krel) )
2646 end do
2647 end if
2648 !*************
2649
2650 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------------- !
2651 ! Cumulus rises upward from 'prel' ( or base interface of 'krel' layer ) !
2652 ! until updraft vertical velocity becomes zero. !
2653 ! Buoyancy sorting is performed via two stages. (1) Using cumulus updraft !
2654 ! properties at the base interface of each layer,perform buoyancy sorting !
2655 ! at the layer mid-point, 'pe', and update cumulus properties at the top !
2656 ! interface, and then (2) by averaging updated cumulus properties at the !
2657 ! top interface and cumulus properties at the base interface, calculate !
2658 ! cumulus updraft properties at pe that will be used in buoyancy sorting !
2659 ! mixing - thlue, qtue and, wue. Using this averaged properties, perform !
2660 ! buoyancy sorting again at pe, and re-calculate fer(k) and fdr(k). Using !
2661 ! this recalculated fer(k) and fdr(k), finally calculate cumulus updraft !
2662 ! properties at the top interface - thlu, qtu, thvu, uu, vu. In the below,!
2663 ! 'iter_xc = 1' performs the first stage, while 'iter_xc= 2' performs the !
2664 ! second stage. We can increase the number of iterations, 'nter_xc'.as we !
2665 ! want, but a sample test indicated that about 3 - 5 iterations produced !
2666 ! satisfactory converent solution. Finally, identify 'kbup' and 'kpen'. !
2667 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------------- !
2668
2669836266210270341 do k = krel, mkx - 1 ! Here, 'k' is a layer index.
2670
26711027034110270341 km1 = k - 1
2672
2673 thlue = thlu(km1)
2674 qtue = qtu(km1)
2675 wue = wu(km1)
2676 wtwb = wtw
2677
26781672765516727655 do iter_xc = 1, niter_xc
2679
26801863533418635334 wtw = wu(km1) * wu(km1)
2681
2682
2683 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------- !
2684 ! Calculate environmental and cumulus saturation 'excess' at 'pe'. !
2685 ! Note that in order to calculate saturation excess, we should use !
2686 ! liquid water temperature instead of temperature as the argument !
2687 ! of "qsat". But note normal argument of "qsat" is temperature. !
2688 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------- !
2689
2690 !NOTE: This section is used purely for buoyancy sorting, and thus
2691 !does not need to be replicated for water tracers - JN.
2692
26931863533418635334 call conden(pe,thle,qte,thj,qvj,qlj,qij,qse,id_check,ncnst)
26941863533418635334 if( id_check .eq. 1 ) then
269500 exit_conden(i) = 1._r8
2696 id_exit = .true.
2697 go to 333
2698 end if
26991863533418635334 thv0j = thj * ( 1._r8 + zvir*qvj - qlj - qij )
2700 rho0j = pe / ( r * thv0j * exne )
2701 qsat_arg = thle*exne
27021863533418635334 call qsat(qsat_arg, pe, es, qs)
27031863533418635334 excess0 = qte - qs
2704
27051863533418635334 call conden(pe,thlue,qtue,thj,qvj,qlj,qij,qse,id_check,ncnst)
27061863533418635334 if( id_check .eq. 1 ) then
270700 exit_conden(i) = 1._r8
2708 id_exit = .true.
2709 go to 333
2710 end if
2711 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
2712 ! Detrain excessive condensate larger than 'criqc' from the cumulus !
2713 ! updraft before performing buoyancy sorting. All I should to do is !
2714 ! to update 'thlue' & 'que' here. Below modification is completely !
2715 ! compatible with the other part of the code since 'thule' & 'qtue' !
2716 ! are used only for buoyancy sorting. I found that as long as I use !
2717 ! 'niter_xc >= 2', detraining excessive condensate before buoyancy !
2718 ! sorting has negligible influence on the buoyancy sorting results. !
2719 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
27201863533418635334 if( (qlj + qij) .gt. criqc ) then
272166604496660449 exql = ( ( qlj + qij ) - criqc ) * qlj / ( qlj + qij )
2722 exqi = ( ( qlj + qij ) - criqc ) * qij / ( qlj + qij )
2723 qtue = qtue - exql - exqi
2724 thlue = thlue + (xlv/cp/exne)*exql + (xls/cp/exne)*exqi
2725 endif
27261863533418635334 call conden(pe,thlue,qtue,thj,qvj,qlj,qij,qse,id_check,ncnst)
27271863533418635334 if( id_check .eq. 1 ) then
272800 exit_conden(i) = 1._r8
2729 id_exit = .true.
2730 go to 333
2731 end if
27321863533418635334 thvj = thj * ( 1._r8 + zvir * qvj - qlj - qij )
2733 tj = thj * exne ! This 'tj' is used for computing thermo. coeffs. below
2734 qsat_arg = thlue*exne
27351863533418635334 call qsat(qsat_arg, pe, es, qs)
27361863533418635334 excessu = qtue - qs
2737
2738 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------- !
2739 ! Calculate critical mixing fraction, 'xc'. Mixture with mixing ratio !
2740 ! smaller than 'xc' will be entrained into cumulus updraft. Both the !
2741 ! saturated updrafts with 'positive buoyancy' or 'negative buoyancy + !
2742 ! strong vertical velocity enough to rise certain threshold distance' !
2743 ! are kept into the updraft in the below program. If the core updraft !
2744 ! is unsaturated, we can set 'xc = 0' and let the cumulus convection !
2745 ! still works or we may exit. !
2746 ! Current below code does not entrain unsaturated mixture. However it !
2747 ! should be modified such that it also entrain unsaturated mixture. !
2748 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------- !
2749
2750 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
2751 ! cridis : Critical stopping distance for buoyancy sorting purpose. !
2752 ! scaleh is only used here. !
2753 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
2754
2755 cridis = rle*scaleh ! Original code
2756 ! cridis = 1._r8*(zs0(k) - zs0(k-1)) ! New code
2757
2758 ! ---------------- !
2759 ! Buoyancy Sorting !
2760 ! ---------------- !
2761
2762 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
2763 ! Case 1 : When both cumulus and env. are unsaturated or saturated. !
2764 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
2765
27661861775637253090 if( ( excessu .le. 0._r8 .and. excess0 .le. 0._r8 ) .or. ( excessu .ge. 0._r8 .and. excess0 .ge. 0._r8 ) ) then
276718945241894524 xc = min(1._r8,max(0._r8,1._r8-2._r8*rbuoy*g*cridis/wue**2._r8*(1._r8-thvj/thv0j)))
2768 ! Below 3 lines are diagnostic output not influencing
2769 ! numerical calculations.
2770 aquad = 0._r8
2771 bquad = 0._r8
2772 cquad = 0._r8
2773 else
2774 ! -------------------------------------------------- !
2775 ! Case 2 : When either cumulus or env. is saturated. !
2776 ! -------------------------------------------------- !
27771674081016740810 xsat = excessu / ( excessu - excess0 );
2778 thlxsat = thlue + xsat * ( thle - thlue );
2779 qtxsat = qtue + xsat * ( qte - qtue );
27801674081016740810 call conden(pe,thlxsat,qtxsat,thj,qvj,qlj,qij,qse,id_check,ncnst)
27811674081016740810 if( id_check .eq. 1 ) then
278200 exit_conden(i) = 1._r8
2783 id_exit = .true.
2784 go to 333
2785 end if
27861674081016740810 thvxsat = thj * ( 1._r8 + zvir * qvj - qlj - qij )
2787 ! -------------------------------------------------- !
2788 ! kk=1 : Cumulus Segment, kk=2 : Environment Segment !
2789 ! -------------------------------------------------- !
27903348162033481620 do kk = 1, 2
27913348162033481620 if( kk .eq. 1 ) then
27921674081016740810 thv_x0 = thvj;
2793 thv_x1 = ( 1._r8 - 1._r8/xsat ) * thvj + ( 1._r8/xsat ) * thvxsat;
2794 else
27951674081016740810 thv_x1 = thv0j;
2796 thv_x0 = ( xsat / ( xsat - 1._r8 ) ) * thv0j + ( 1._r8/( 1._r8 - xsat ) ) * thvxsat;
2797 endif
27983348162033481620 aquad = wue**2;
2799 bquad = 2._r8*rbuoy*g*cridis*(thv_x1 - thv_x0)/thv0j - 2._r8*wue**2;
2800 cquad = 2._r8*rbuoy*g*cridis*(thv_x0 - thv0j)/thv0j + wue**2;
2801 if( kk .eq. 1 ) then
28021674081016740810 if( ( bquad**2-4._r8*aquad*cquad ) .ge. 0._r8 ) then
28031674081016740810 call roots(aquad,bquad,cquad,xs1,xs2,status)
28041674081016740810 x_cu = min(1._r8,max(0._r8,min(xsat,min(xs1,xs2))))
2805 else
280600 x_cu = xsat;
2807 endif
2808 else
28091674081016740810 if( ( bquad**2-4._r8*aquad*cquad) .ge. 0._r8 ) then
28101674081016740810 call roots(aquad,bquad,cquad,xs1,xs2,status)
28111674081016740810 x_en = min(1._r8,max(0._r8,max(xsat,min(xs1,xs2))))
2812 else
281300 x_en = 1._r8;
2814 endif
2815 endif
2816 enddo
28171674081016740810 if( x_cu .eq. xsat ) then
2818956763956763 xc = max(x_cu, x_en);
2819 else
28201578404715784047 xc = x_cu;
2821 endif
2822 endif
2823
2824 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
2825 ! Compute fractional lateral entrainment & detrainment rate in each layers.!
2826 ! The unit of rei(k), fer(k), and fdr(k) is [Pa-1]. Alternative choice of !
2827 ! 'rei(k)' is also shown below, where coefficient 0.5 was from approximate !
2828 ! tuning against the BOMEX case. !
2829 ! In order to prevent the onset of instability in association with cumulus !
2830 ! induced subsidence advection, cumulus mass flux at the top interface in !
2831 ! any layer should be smaller than ( 90% of ) total mass within that layer.!
2832 ! I imposed limits on 'rei(k)' as below, in such that stability condition !
2833 ! is always satisfied. !
2834 ! Below limiter of 'rei(k)' becomes negative for some cases, causing error.!
2835 ! So, for the time being, I came back to the original limiter. !
2836 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
28371863533418635334 ee2 = xc**2
2838 ud2 = 1._r8 - 2._r8*xc + xc**2
2839 ! rei(k) = ( rkm / scaleh / g / rho0j ) ! Default.
2840 rei(k) = ( 0.5_r8 * rkm / z0(k) / g /rho0j ) ! Alternative.
2841574131811482636 if( xc .gt. 0.5_r8 ) rei(k) = min(rei(k),0.9_r8*log(dp0(k)/g/dt/umf(km1) + 1._r8)/dpe/(2._r8*xc-1._r8))
28421863533418635334 fer(k) = rei(k) * ee2
2843 fdr(k) = rei(k) * ud2
2844
2845 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
2846 ! Iteration Start due to 'maxufrc' constraint [ ****************************** ] !
2847 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
2848
2849 ! -------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
2850 ! Calculate cumulus updraft mass flux and penetrative entrainment mass flux. !
2851 ! Note that non-zero penetrative entrainment mass flux will be asigned only !
2852 ! to interfaces from the top interface of 'kbup' layer to the base interface !
2853 ! of 'kpen' layer as will be shown later. !
2854 ! -------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
2855
28561863533418635334 umf(k) = umf(km1) * exp( dpe * ( fer(k) - fdr(k) ) )
2857 emf(k) = 0._r8
2858
2859 ! --------------------------------------------------------- !
2860 ! Compute cumulus updraft properties at the top interface. !
2861 ! Also use Tayler expansion in order to treat limiting case !
2862 ! --------------------------------------------------------- !
2863
2864 if( fer(k)*dpe .lt. 1.e-4_r8 ) then
286513363381336338 thlu(k) = thlu(km1) + ( thle + ssthl0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 - thlu(km1) ) * fer(k) * dpe
2866 qtu(k) = qtu(km1) + ( qte + ssqt0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 - qtu(km1) ) * fer(k) * dpe
2867 uu(k) = uu(km1) + ( ue + ssu0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 - uu(km1) ) * fer(k) * dpe - PGFc * ssu0(k) * dpe
2868 vu(k) = vu(km1) + ( ve + ssv0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 - vu(km1) ) * fer(k) * dpe - PGFc * ssv0(k) * dpe
28697617126676171266 do m = 1, ncnst !<-Handles water tracers
2870 tru(k,m) = tru(km1,m) + ( tre(m) + sstr0(k,m) * dpe / 2._r8 - tru(km1,m) ) * fer(k) * dpe
2871 enddo
2872 !*************
2873 !Water tracers
2874 !*************
287513363381336338 if(trace_water) then
287653453526681690 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
2877 wtu(k,m) = wtu(km1,m) + ( wte(m) + sswt0(k,m) * dpe / 2._r8 - wtu(km1,m) ) * fer(k) * dpe
2878 end do
2879 end if
2880 !*************
2881 else
28821729899617298996 thlu(k) = ( thle + ssthl0(k) / fer(k) - ssthl0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 ) - &
2883 ( thle + ssthl0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 - thlu(km1) + ssthl0(k) / fer(k) ) * exp(-fer(k) * dpe)
28841729899617298996 qtu(k) = ( qte + ssqt0(k) / fer(k) - ssqt0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 ) - &
2885 ( qte + ssqt0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 - qtu(km1) + ssqt0(k) / fer(k) ) * exp(-fer(k) * dpe)
28861729899617298996 uu(k) = ( ue + ( 1._r8 - PGFc ) * ssu0(k) / fer(k) - ssu0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 ) - &
2887 ( ue + ssu0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 - uu(km1) + ( 1._r8 - PGFc ) * ssu0(k) / fer(k) ) * exp(-fer(k) * dpe)
28881729899617298996 vu(k) = ( ve + ( 1._r8 - PGFc ) * ssv0(k) / fer(k) - ssv0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 ) - &
2889 ( ve + ssv0(k) * dpe / 2._r8 - vu(km1) + ( 1._r8 - PGFc ) * ssv0(k) / fer(k) ) * exp(-fer(k) * dpe)
2890986042772986042772 do m = 1, ncnst !<-Handles water tracers
2891 tru(k,m) = ( tre(m) + sstr0(k,m) / fer(k) - sstr0(k,m) * dpe / 2._r8 ) - &
2892 ( tre(m) + sstr0(k,m) * dpe / 2._r8 - tru(km1,m) + sstr0(k,m) / fer(k) ) * exp(-fer(k) * dpe)
2893 enddo
2894 !*************
2895 !Water tracers
2896 !*************
28971729899617298996 if(trace_water) then
28986919598486494980 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
2899 wtu(k,m) = ( wte(m) + sswt0(k,m) / fer(k) - sswt0(k,m) * dpe / 2._r8 ) - &
2900 ( wte(m) + sswt0(k,m) * dpe / 2._r8 - wtu(km1,m) + sswt0(k,m) / fer(k) ) * exp(-fer(k) * dpe)
2901 end do
2902 end if
2903 !*************
2904 end if
2905
2906 !------------------------------------------------------------------- !
2907 ! Expel some of cloud water and ice from cumulus updraft at the top !
2908 ! interface. Note that this is not 'detrainment' term but a 'sink' !
2909 ! term of cumulus updraft qt ( or one part of 'source' term of mean !
2910 ! environmental qt ). At this stage, as the most simplest choice, if !
2911 ! condensate amount within cumulus updraft is larger than a critical !
2912 ! value, 'criqc', expels the surplus condensate from cumulus updraft !
2913 ! to the environment. A certain fraction ( e.g., 'frc_sus' ) of this !
2914 ! expelled condesnate will be in a form that can be suspended in the !
2915 ! layer k where it was formed, while the other fraction, '1-frc_sus' !
2916 ! will be in a form of precipitatble (e.g.,can potentially fall down !
2917 ! across the base interface of layer k ). In turn we should describe !
2918 ! subsequent falling of precipitable condensate ('1-frc_sus') across !
2919 ! the base interface of the layer k, & evaporation of precipitating !
2920 ! water in the below layer k-1 and associated evaporative cooling of !
2921 ! the later, k-1, and falling of 'non-evaporated precipitating water !
2922 ! ( which was initially formed in layer k ) and a newly-formed preci !
2923 ! pitable water in the layer, k-1', across the base interface of the !
2924 ! lower layer k-1. Cloud microphysics should correctly describe all !
2925 ! of these process. In a near future, I should significantly modify !
2926 ! this cloud microphysics, including precipitation-induced downdraft !
2927 ! also. !
2928 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------ !
2929
29301863533418635334 if(trace_water) then
2931223624008428612682 wtout(:,:) = 0.0_r8
293274541336186353340 call conden(ps0(k),thlu(k),qtu(k),thj,qvj,qlj,qij,qse,id_check,wtrc_nwset,qv0=qtu(k),tr0=wtu(k,:),wtout=wtout)
2933 else
293400 call conden(ps0(k),thlu(k),qtu(k),thj,qvj,qlj,qij,qse,id_check,ncnst)
2935 end if
2936
29371863533418635334 if( id_check .eq. 1 ) then
293800 exit_conden(i) = 1._r8
2939 id_exit = .true.
2940 go to 333
2941 end if
29421863533418635334 if( (qlj + qij) .gt. criqc ) then
294387800098780009 exql = ( ( qlj + qij ) - criqc ) * qlj / ( qlj + qij )
2944 exqi = ( ( qlj + qij ) - criqc ) * qij / ( qlj + qij )
2945 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------- !
2946 ! It is very important to re-update 'qtu' and 'thlu' at the upper !
2947 ! interface after expelling condensate from cumulus updraft at the !
2948 ! top interface of the layer. As mentioned above, this is a 'sink' !
2949 ! of cumulus qt (or equivalently, a 'source' of environmentasl qt),!
2950 ! not a regular convective'detrainment'. !
2951 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------- !
2952 qtu(k) = qtu(k) - exql - exqi
2953 thlu(k) = thlu(k) + (xlv/cp/exns0(k))*exql + (xls/cp/exns0(k))*exqi
2954 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------- !
2955 ! Expelled cloud condensate into the environment from the updraft. !
2956 ! After all the calculation later, 'dwten' and 'diten' will have a !
2957 ! unit of [ kg/kg/s ], because it is a tendency of qt. Restoration !
2958 ! of 'dwten' and 'diten' to this correct unit through multiplying !
2959 ! 'umf(k)*g/dp0(k)' will be performed later after finally updating !
2960 ! 'umf' using a 'rmaxfrac' constraint near the end of this updraft !
2961 ! buoyancy sorting loop. !
2962 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------- !
2963 dwten(k) = exql
2964 diten(k) = exqi
2965
2966 if(trace_water) then
2967 !**********************************************************
2968 !Generate condensate detrainment for water tracers/isotopes
2969 !**********************************************************
2970 !Method one: Calculate condensate ratio, and adjust detrainment
2971 !values accordingly. - JN
29723512003643900045 do m=1,wtrc_nwset !Loop over water species
2973
29743512003670240072 Rldt = wtrc_ratio(iwspec(wtrc_iatype(m,iwtliq)),wtout(m,2),&
2975 wtout(1,2)) !Calculate liquid ratio
29763512003635120036 Ridt = wtrc_ratio(iwspec(wtrc_iatype(m,iwtice)),wtout(m,3),&
2977 wtout(1,3)) !Calculate ice ratio
2978
2979 wtexql(m) = Rldt*exql !Modify detrainment by tracer ratio
2980 wtexqi(m) = Ridt*exqi
2981
2982 !Remove detrained condensate from updraft values:
2983 tru(k,wtrc_iatype(m,iwtliq)) = tru(k,wtrc_iatype(m,iwtliq)) - wtexql(m)
2984 tru(k,wtrc_iatype(m,iwtice)) = tru(k,wtrc_iatype(m,iwtice)) - wtexqi(m)
2985
2986 wtu(k,m) = wtu(k,m) - wtexql(m) - wtexqi(m)
2987
2988 !Add detrained condensate to detrainment tendency:
2989 wtdwten(k,m) = wtexql(m)
2990 wtditen(k,m) = wtexqi(m)
2991 end do
2992 !**********************************************************
2993 end if
2994
2995 else
299698553259855325 dwten(k) = 0._r8
2997 diten(k) = 0._r8
2998
2999 !Water tracers:
30003942130059131950 wtdwten(k,:) = 0._r8
30013942130059131950 wtditen(k,:) = 0._r8
3002 endif
3003 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
3004 ! Update 'thvu(k)' after detraining condensate from cumulus updraft.!
3005 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
3006
3007 !NOTE: This condensation appears to be used solely for thermodynamics, and thus
3008 !does not need to be replicated. - JN.
3009
30101863533418635334 call conden(ps0(k),thlu(k),qtu(k),thj,qvj,qlj,qij,qse,id_check,ncnst)
30111863533418635334 if( id_check .eq. 1 ) then
301200 exit_conden(i) = 1._r8
3013 id_exit = .true.
3014 go to 333
3015 end if
30161863533418635334 thvu(k) = thj * ( 1._r8 + zvir * qvj - qlj - qij )
3017
3018 ! ----------------------------------------------------------- !
3019 ! Calculate updraft vertical velocity at the upper interface. !
3020 ! In order to calculate 'wtw' at the upper interface, we use !
3021 ! 'wtw' at the lower interface. Note 'wtw' is continuously !
3022 ! updated as cumulus updraft rises. !
3023 ! ----------------------------------------------------------- !
3024
3025 bogbot = rbuoy * ( thvu(km1) / thvebot - 1._r8 ) ! Cloud buoyancy at base interface
3026 bogtop = rbuoy * ( thvu(k) / thv0top(k) - 1._r8 ) ! Cloud buoyancy at top interface
3027
3028 delbog = bogtop - bogbot
3029 drage = fer(k) * ( 1._r8 + rdrag )
30301863533418635334 expfac = exp(-2._r8*drage*dpe)
3031
3032 wtwb = wtw
3033 if( drage*dpe .gt. 1.e-3_r8 ) then
30341724120617241206 wtw = wtw*expfac + (delbog + (1._r8-expfac)*(bogbot + delbog/(-2._r8*drage*dpe)))/(rho0j*drage)
3035 else
303613941281394128 wtw = wtw + dpe * ( bogbot + bogtop ) / rho0j
3037 endif
3038
3039 ! Force the plume rise at least to klfc of the undiluted plume.
3040 ! Because even the below is not complete, I decided not to include this.
3041
3042 ! if( k .le. klfc ) then
3043 ! wtw = max( 1.e-2_r8, wtw )
3044 ! endif
3045
3046 ! -------------------------------------------------------------- !
3047 ! Repeat 'iter_xc' iteration loop until 'iter_xc = niter_xc'. !
3048 ! Also treat the case even when wtw < 0 at the 'kpen' interface. !
3049 ! -------------------------------------------------------------- !
3050
30511863533418635334 if( wtw .gt. 0._r8 ) then
30521672765516727655 thlue = 0.5_r8 * ( thlu(km1) + thlu(k) )
3053 qtue = 0.5_r8 * ( qtu(km1) + qtu(k) )
30541672765516727655 wue = 0.5_r8 * sqrt( max( wtwb + wtw, 0._r8 ) )
3055 else
3056 go to 111
3057 endif
3058
3059 enddo ! End of 'iter_xc' loop
3060
3061 111 continue
3062
3063 ! --------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3064 ! Add the contribution of self-detrainment to vertical variations of cumulus !
3065 ! updraft mass flux. The reason why we are trying to include self-detrainment !
3066 ! is as follows. In current scheme, vertical variation of updraft mass flux !
3067 ! is not fully consistent with the vertical variation of updraft vertical w. !
3068 ! For example, within a given layer, let's assume that cumulus w is positive !
3069 ! at the base interface, while negative at the top interface. This means that !
3070 ! cumulus updraft cannot reach to the top interface of the layer. However, !
3071 ! cumulus updraft mass flux at the top interface is not zero according to the !
3072 ! vertical tendency equation of cumulus mass flux. Ideally, cumulus updraft !
3073 ! mass flux at the top interface should be zero for this case. In order to !
3074 ! assures that cumulus updraft mass flux goes to zero when cumulus updraft !
3075 ! vertical velocity goes to zero, we are imposing self-detrainment term as !
3076 ! below by considering layer-mean cloud buoyancy and cumulus updraft vertical !
3077 ! velocity square at the top interface. Use of auto-detrainment term will be !
3078 ! determined by setting 'use_self_detrain=.true.' in the parameter sentence. !
3079 ! --------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3080
30811027034110270341 if( use_self_detrain ) then
3082 autodet = min( 0.5_r8*g*(bogbot+bogtop)/(max(wtw,0._r8)+1.e-4_r8), 0._r8 )
308300 umf(k) = umf(k) * exp( 0.637_r8*(dpe/rho0j/g) * autodet )
3084 end if
30851027034110270341 if( umf(k) .eq. 0._r8 ) wtw = -1._r8
3086
3087 ! -------------------------------------- !
3088 ! Below block is just a dignostic output !
3089 ! -------------------------------------- !
3090
30911027034110270341 excessu_arr(k) = excessu
3092 excess0_arr(k) = excess0
3093 xc_arr(k) = xc
3094 aquad_arr(k) = aquad
3095 bquad_arr(k) = bquad
3096 cquad_arr(K) = cquad
3097 bogbot_arr(k) = bogbot
3098 bogtop_arr(k) = bogtop
3099
3100 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3101 ! 'kbup' is the upper most layer in which cloud buoyancy is positive !
3102 ! both at the base and top interface. 'kpen' is the upper most layer !
3103 ! up to cumulus can reach. Usually, 'kpen' is located higher than the !
3104 ! 'kbup'. Note we initialized these by 'kbup = krel' & 'kpen = krel'. !
3105 ! As explained before, it is possible that only 'kpen' is updated, !
3106 ! while 'kbup' keeps its initialization value. For this case, current !
3107 ! scheme will simply turns-off penetrative entrainment fluxes and use !
3108 ! normal buoyancy-sorting fluxes for 'kbup <= k <= kpen-1' interfaces,!
3109 ! in order to describe shallow continental cumulus convection. !
3110 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3111
3112 ! if( bogbot .gt. 0._r8 .and. bogtop .gt. 0._r8 ) then
3113 ! if( bogtop .gt. 0._r8 ) then
311480874598087459 if( bogtop .gt. 0._r8 .and. wtw .gt. 0._r8 ) then
311580440928044092 kbup = k
3116 end if
3117
31181027034110270341 if( wtw .le. 0._r8 ) then
311919076791907679 kpen = k
3120 go to 45
3121 end if
3122
312383626628362662 wu(k) = sqrt(wtw)
3124 if( wu(k) .gt. 100._r8 ) then
312500 exit_wu(i) = 1._r8
3126 id_exit = .true.
3127 go to 333
3128 endif
3129
3130 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3131 ! Iteration end due to 'rmaxfrac' constraint [ ***************************** ] !
3132 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3133
3134 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3135 ! Calculate updraft fractional area at the upper interface and set upper !
3136 ! limit to 'ufrc' by 'rmaxfrac'. In order to keep the consistency among !
3137 ! ['ufrc','umf','wu (or wtw)'], if ufrc is limited by 'rmaxfrac', either !
3138 ! 'umf' or 'wu' should be changed. Although both 'umf' and 'wu (wtw)' at !
3139 ! the current upper interface are used for updating 'umf' & 'wu' at the !
3140 ! next upper interface, 'umf' is a passive variable not influencing the !
3141 ! buoyancy sorting process in contrast to 'wtw'. This is a reason why we !
3142 ! adjusted 'umf' instead of 'wtw'. In turn we updated 'fdr' here instead !
3143 ! of 'fer', which guarantees that all previously updated thermodynamic !
3144 ! variables at the upper interface before applying 'rmaxfrac' constraint !
3145 ! are already internally consistent, even though 'ufrc' is limited by !
3146 ! 'rmaxfrac'. Thus, we don't need to go through interation loop again.If !
3147 ! If we update 'fer' however, we should go through above iteration loop. !
3148 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3149
315083626628362662 rhos0j = ps0(k) / ( r * 0.5_r8 * ( thv0bot(k+1) + thv0top(k) ) * exns0(k) )
3151 ufrc(k) = umf(k) / ( rhos0j * wu(k) )
3152 if( ufrc(k) .gt. rmaxfrac ) then
315311069861106986 limit_ufrc(i) = 1._r8
3154 ufrc(k) = rmaxfrac
3155 umf(k) = rmaxfrac * rhos0j * wu(k)
315611069862213972 fdr(k) = fer(k) - log( umf(k) / umf(km1) ) / dpe
3157 endif
3158
3159 ! ------------------------------------------------------------ !
3160 ! Update environmental properties for at the mid-point of next !
3161 ! upper layer for use in buoyancy sorting. !
3162 ! ------------------------------------------------------------ !
3163
316483626628362662 pe = p0(k+1)
3165 dpe = dp0(k+1)
3166 exne = exn0(k+1)
3167 thvebot = thv0bot(k+1)
3168 thle = thl0(k+1)
3169 qte = qt0(k+1)
3170 ue = u0(k+1)
3171 ve = v0(k+1)
3172476671734476671734 do m = 1, ncnst
3173 tre(m) = tr0(k+1,m) !<-Water tracers handled here (may need to modify).
3174 enddo
3175
3176 !*************
3177 !Water tracers
3178 !*************
317983626628362662 if(trace_water) then
31803345064841813310 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
3181 wte(m) = wt0(k+1,m)
3182 end do
3183 end if
3184 !*************
3185
3186 end do ! End of cumulus updraft loop from the 'krel' layer to 'kpen' layer.
3187
3188 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3189 ! Up to this point, we finished all of buoyancy sorting processes from the 'krel' !
3190 ! layer to 'kpen' layer: at the top interface of individual layers, we calculated !
3191 ! updraft and penetrative mass fluxes [ umf(k) & emf(k) = 0 ], updraft fractional !
3192 ! area [ ufrc(k) ], updraft vertical velocity [ wu(k) ], updraft thermodynamic !
3193 ! variables [thlu(k),qtu(k),uu(k),vu(k),thvu(k)]. In the layer,we also calculated !
3194 ! fractional entrainment-detrainment rate [ fer(k), fdr(k) ], and detrainment ten !
3195 ! dency of water and ice from cumulus updraft [ dwten(k), diten(k) ]. In addition,!
3196 ! we updated and identified 'krel' and 'kpen' layer index, if any. In the 'kpen' !
3197 ! layer, we calculated everything mentioned above except the 'wu(k)' and 'ufrc(k)'!
3198 ! since a real value of updraft vertical velocity is not defined at the kpen top !
3199 ! interface (note 'ufrc' at the top interface of layer is calculated from 'umf(k)'!
3200 ! and 'wu(k)'). As mentioned before, special treatment is required when 'kbup' is !
3201 ! not updated and so 'kbup = krel'. !
3202 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3203
3204 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3205 ! During the 'iter_scaleh' iteration loop, non-physical ( with non-zero values ) !
3206 ! values can remain in the variable arrays above (also 'including' in case of wu !
3207 ! and ufrc at the top interface) the 'kpen' layer. This can happen when the kpen !
3208 ! layer index identified from the 'iter_scaleh = 1' iteration loop is located at !
3209 ! above the kpen layer index identified from 'iter_scaleh = 3' iteration loop. !
3210 ! Thus, in the following calculations, we should only use the values in each !
3211 ! variables only up to finally identified 'kpen' layer & 'kpen' interface except !
3212 ! 'wu' and 'ufrc' at the top interface of 'kpen' layer. Note that in order to !
3213 ! prevent any problems due to these non-physical values, I re-initialized the !
3214 ! values of [ umf(kpen:mkx), emf(kpen:mkx), dwten(kpen+1:mkx), diten(kpen+1:mkx),!
3215 ! fer(kpen:mkx), fdr(kpen+1:mkx), ufrc(kpen:mkx) ] to be zero after 'iter_scaleh'!
3216 ! do loop. !
3217 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3218
3219 45 continue
3220
3221 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3222 ! Calculate 'ppen( < 0 )', updarft penetrative distance from the lower interface !
3223 ! of 'kpen' layer. Note that bogbot & bogtop at the 'kpen' layer either when fer !
3224 ! is zero or non-zero was already calculated above. !
3225 ! It seems that below qudarature solving formula is valid only when bogbot < 0. !
3226 ! Below solving equation is clearly wrong ! I should revise this ! !
3227 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3228
322919076791907679 if( drage .eq. 0._r8 ) then
323010667481066748 aquad = ( bogtop - bogbot ) / ( ps0(kpen) - ps0(kpen-1) )
3231 bquad = 2._r8 * bogbot
3232 cquad = -wu(kpen-1)**2 * rho0j
323310667481066748 call roots(aquad,bquad,cquad,xc1,xc2,status)
323410667481066748 if( status .eq. 0 ) then
323510667481275321 if( xc1 .le. 0._r8 .and. xc2 .le. 0._r8 ) then
3236154099154099 ppen = max( xc1, xc2 )
3237 ppen = min( 0._r8,max( -dp0(kpen), ppen ) )
32389126491770824 elseif( xc1 .gt. 0._r8 .and. xc2 .gt. 0._r8 ) then
323900 ppen = -dp0(kpen)
324000 write(iulog,*) 'Warning : UW-Cumulus penetrates upto kpen interface'
3241 else
3242912649912649 ppen = min( xc1, xc2 )
3243 ppen = min( 0._r8,max( -dp0(kpen), ppen ) )
3244 endif
3245 else
324600 ppen = -dp0(kpen)
324700 write(iulog,*) 'Warning : UW-Cumulus penetrates upto kpen interface'
3248 endif
3249 else
32508409311681862 ppen = compute_ppen(wtwb,drage,bogbot,bogtop,rho0j,dp0(kpen))
3251 endif
325219076793815362 if( ppen .eq. -dp0(kpen) .or. ppen .eq. 0._r8 ) limit_ppen(i) = 1._r8
3253
3254 ! -------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3255 ! Re-calculate the amount of expelled condensate from cloud updraft !
3256 ! at the cumulus top. This is necessary for refined calculations of !
3257 ! bulk cloud microphysics at the cumulus top. Note that ppen < 0._r8 !
3258 ! In the below, I explicitly calculate 'thlu_top' & 'qtu_top' by !
3259 ! using non-zero 'fer(kpen)'. !
3260 ! -------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3261
326219076791907679 if( fer(kpen)*(-ppen) .lt. 1.e-4_r8 ) then
326310855761085576 thlu_top = thlu(kpen-1) + ( thl0(kpen) + ssthl0(kpen) * (-ppen) / 2._r8 - thlu(kpen-1) ) * fer(kpen) * (-ppen)
3264 qtu_top = qtu(kpen-1) + ( qt0(kpen) + ssqt0(kpen) * (-ppen) / 2._r8 - qtu(kpen-1) ) * fer(kpen) * (-ppen)
3265 !Water tracers:
3266 !*************
3267 if(trace_water) then
326843423045427880 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
3269 wtu_top(m) = wtu(kpen-1,m) + ( wt0(kpen,m) + sswt0(kpen,m) * &
3270 (-ppen) / 2._r8 - wtu(kpen-1,m) ) * fer(kpen) * (-ppen)
3271 end do
3272 end if
3273 !*************
3274 else
3275822103822103 thlu_top = ( thl0(kpen) + ssthl0(kpen) / fer(kpen) - ssthl0(kpen) * (-ppen) / 2._r8 ) - &
3276 ( thl0(kpen) + ssthl0(kpen) * (-ppen) / 2._r8 - thlu(kpen-1) + ssthl0(kpen) / fer(kpen) ) &
3277 * exp(-fer(kpen) * (-ppen))
3278822103822103 qtu_top = ( qt0(kpen) + ssqt0(kpen) / fer(kpen) - ssqt0(kpen) * (-ppen) / 2._r8 ) - &
3279 ( qt0(kpen) + ssqt0(kpen) * (-ppen) / 2._r8 - qtu(kpen-1) + ssqt0(kpen) / fer(kpen) ) &
3280 * exp(-fer(kpen) * (-ppen))
3281 !Water tracers:
3282 !*************
3283 if(trace_water) then
328432884124110515 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
3285 wtu_top(m) = ( wt0(kpen,m) + sswt0(kpen,m) / fer(kpen) - sswt0(kpen,m) * (-ppen) / 2._r8 ) - &
3286 ( wt0(kpen,m) + sswt0(kpen,m) * (-ppen) / 2._r8 - wtu(kpen-1,m) + sswt0(kpen,m) / fer(kpen) ) &
3287 * exp(-fer(kpen) * (-ppen))
3288 end do
3289 end if
3290 !*************
3291 end if
3292
3293 !NOTE: Not 100% sure if using qv0/tr0 to calculate R is appropriate here
3294 !(versus some sort of updraft quantity) - JN
3295
329619076791907679 if(trace_water) then
32972289214843876617 wtout(:,:) = 0._r8
329819076791907679 call conden(ps0(kpen-1)+ppen,thlu_top,qtu_top,thj,qvj,qlj,qij,qse, &
3299 id_check,wtrc_nwset,qv0=qtu_top,tr0=wtu_top(:),wtout=wtout)
3300 else
330100 call conden(ps0(kpen-1)+ppen,thlu_top,qtu_top,thj,qvj,qlj,qij,qse,id_check,ncnst)
3302 end if
330319076791907679 if( id_check .eq. 1 ) then
330400 exit_conden(i) = 1._r8
3305 id_exit = .true.
3306 go to 333
3307 end if
330819076793815358 exntop = ((ps0(kpen-1)+ppen)/p00)**rovcp
3309 if( (qlj + qij) .gt. criqc ) then
3310931735931735 dwten(kpen) = ( ( qlj + qij ) - criqc ) * qlj / ( qlj + qij )
3311 diten(kpen) = ( ( qlj + qij ) - criqc ) * qij / ( qlj + qij )
3312 qtu_top = qtu_top - dwten(kpen) - diten(kpen)
3313 thlu_top = thlu_top + (xlv/cp/exntop)*dwten(kpen) + (xls/cp/exntop)*diten(kpen)
3314
3315 if(trace_water) then
3316 !*********************************************
3317 !Re-calculate water tracer expelled condensate
3318 !*********************************************
3319
3320 !Method one: Calculate condensate ratio, and adjust detrainment
3321 !values accordingly. - JN
3322
332337269404658675 do m=1,wtrc_nwset !Loop over water species
3324
332537269407453880 Rldt = wtrc_ratio(iwspec(wtrc_iatype(m,iwtliq)),wtout(m,2),&
3326 wtout(1,2)) !Calculate liquid ratio
332737269403726940 Ridt = wtrc_ratio(iwspec(wtrc_iatype(m,iwtice)),wtout(m,3),&
3328 wtout(1,3)) !Calculate ice ratio
3329
3330 !Add detrained condensate to detrainment tendency:
3331 wtdwten(kpen,m) = Rldt*dwten(kpen)
3332 wtditen(kpen,m) = Ridt*diten(kpen)
3333
3334 !Remove detrained condensate from updraft values:
3335 wtu_top(m) = wtu_top(m)-wtdwten(kpen,m) - wtditen(kpen,m)
3336
3337 end do
3338 !*********************************************
3339 end if
3340
3341 else
3342975944975944 dwten(kpen) = 0._r8
3343 diten(kpen) = 0._r8
3344 !Water tracers:
3345 !*************
3346 if(trace_water) then
334739037765855664 wtdwten(kpen,:) = 0._r8
334839037765855664 wtditen(kpen,:) = 0._r8
3349 end if
3350 !************
3351 endif
3352
3353
3354 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3355 ! Calculate cumulus scale height as the top height that cumulus can reach.!
3356 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3357
3358 rhos0j = ps0(kpen-1)/(r*0.5_r8*(thv0bot(kpen)+thv0top(kpen-1))*exns0(kpen-1))
3359 cush = zs0(kpen-1) - ppen/rhos0j/g
3360 scaleh = cush
3361
3362 end do ! End of 'iter_scaleh' loop.
3363
3364 ! -------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3365 ! The 'forcedCu' is logical identifier saying whether cumulus updraft !
3366 ! overcome the buoyancy barrier just above the PBL top. If it is true, !
3367 ! cumulus did not overcome the barrier - this is a shallow convection !
3368 ! with negative cloud buoyancy, mimicking shallow continental cumulus !
3369 ! convection. Depending on 'forcedCu' parameter, treatment of heat & !
3370 ! moisture fluxes at the entraining interfaces, 'kbup <= k < kpen - 1' !
3371 ! will be set up in a different ways, as will be shown later. !
3372 ! -------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3373
3374635893635893 if( kbup .eq. krel ) then
33754825848258 forcedCu = .true.
3376 limit_shcu(i) = 1._r8
3377 else
3378587635587635 forcedCu = .false.
3379 limit_shcu(i) = 0._r8
3380 endif
3381
3382 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3383 ! Filtering of unerasonable cumulus adjustment here. This is a very !
3384 ! important process which should be done cautiously. Various ways of !
3385 ! filtering are possible depending on cases mainly using the indices !
3386 ! of key layers - 'klcl','kinv','krel','klfc','kbup','kpen'. At this !
3387 ! stage, the followings are all possible : 'kinv >= 2', 'klcl >= 1', !
3388 ! 'krel >= kinv', 'kbup >= krel', 'kpen >= krel'. I must design this !
3389 ! filtering very cautiously, in such that none of realistic cumulus !
3390 ! convection is arbitrarily turned-off. Potentially, I might turn-off!
3391 ! cumulus convection if layer-mean 'ql > 0' in the 'kinv-1' layer,in !
3392 ! order to suppress cumulus convection growing, based at the Sc top. !
3393 ! This is one of potential future modifications. Note that ppen < 0. !
3394 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3395
3396635893635893 cldhgt = ps0(kpen-1) + ppen
3397 if( forcedCu ) then
3398 ! write(iulog,*) 'forcedCu - did not overcome initial buoyancy barrier'
33994825848258 exit_cufilter(i) = 1._r8
3400 id_exit = .true.
3401 go to 333
3402 end if
3403 ! Limit 'additional shallow cumulus' for DYCOMS simulation.
3404 ! if( cldhgt.ge.88000._r8 ) then
3405 ! id_exit = .true.
3406 ! go to 333
3407 ! end if
3408
3409 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3410 ! Re-initializing some key variables above the 'kpen' layer in order to suppress !
3411 ! the influence of non-physical values above 'kpen', in association with the use !
3412 ! of 'iter_scaleh' loop. Note that umf, emf, ufrc are defined at the interfaces !
3413 ! (0:mkx), while 'dwten','diten', 'fer', 'fdr' are defined at layer mid-points. !
3414 ! Initialization of 'fer' and 'fdr' is for correct writing purpose of diagnostic !
3415 ! output. Note that we set umf(kpen)=emf(kpen)=ufrc(kpen)=0, in consistent with !
3416 ! wtw < 0 at the top interface of 'kpen' layer. However, we still have non-zero !
3417 ! expelled cloud condensate in the 'kpen' layer. !
3418 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3419
34201278120013956470 umf(kpen:mkx) = 0._r8
34211278120013956470 emf(kpen:mkx) = 0._r8
34221278120013956470 ufrc(kpen:mkx) = 0._r8
34231219356513368835 dwten(kpen+1:mkx) = 0._r8
34241219356513368835 diten(kpen+1:mkx) = 0._r8
34251219356513368835 fer(kpen+1:mkx) = 0._r8
34261219356513368835 fdr(kpen+1:mkx) = 0._r8
3427
3428 !Water tracers:
3429 !*************
3430587635587635 if(trace_water) then
34314877426057001150 wtdwten(kpen+1:mkx,:) = 0._r8
34324877426057001150 wtditen(kpen+1:mkx,:) = 0._r8
3433 end if
3434 !*************
3435
3436 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3437 ! Calculate downward penetrative entrainment mass flux, 'emf(k) < 0', and !
3438 ! thermodynamic properties of penetratively entrained airs at entraining !
3439 ! interfaces. emf(k) is defined from the top interface of the layer kbup !
3440 ! to the bottom interface of the layer 'kpen'. Note even when kbup = krel,!
3441 ! i.e.,even when 'kbup' was not updated in the above buoyancy sorting do !
3442 ! loop (i.e., 'kbup' remains as the initialization value), below do loop !
3443 ! of penetrative entrainment flux can be performed without any conceptual !
3444 ! or logical problems, because we have already computed all the variables !
3445 ! necessary for performing below penetrative entrainment block. !
3446 ! In the below 'do' loop, 'k' is an interface index at which non-zero 'emf'!
3447 ! (penetrative entrainment mass flux) is calculated. Since cumulus updraft !
3448 ! is negatively buoyant in the layers between the top interface of 'kbup' !
3449 ! layer (interface index, kbup) and the top interface of 'kpen' layer, the !
3450 ! fractional lateral entrainment, fer(k) within these layers will be close !
3451 ! to zero - so it is likely that only strong lateral detrainment occurs in !
3452 ! thses layers. Under this situation,we can easily calculate the amount of !
3453 ! detrainment cumulus air into these negatively buoyanct layers by simply !
3454 ! comparing cumulus updraft mass fluxes between the base and top interface !
3455 ! of each layer: emf(k) = emf(k-1)*exp(-fdr(k)*dp0(k)) !
3456 ! ~ emf(k-1)*(1-rei(k)*dp0(k)) !
3457 ! emf(k-1)-emf(k) ~ emf(k-1)*rei(k)*dp0(k) !
3458 ! Current code assumes that about 'rpen~10' times of these detrained mass !
3459 ! are penetratively re-entrained down into the 'k-1' interface. And all of !
3460 ! these detrained masses are finally dumped down into the top interface of !
3461 ! 'kbup' layer. Thus, the amount of penetratively entrained air across the !
3462 ! top interface of 'kbup' layer with 'rpen~10' becomes too large. !
3463 ! Note that this penetrative entrainment part can be completely turned-off !
3464 ! and we can simply use normal buoyancy-sorting involved turbulent fluxes !
3465 ! by modifying 'penetrative entrainment fluxes' part below. !
3466 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3467
3468 ! -----------------------------------------------------------------------!
3469 ! Calculate entrainment mass flux and conservative scalars of entraining !
3470 ! free air at interfaces of 'kbup <= k < kpen - 1' !
3471 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3472
34731821668518804320 do k = 0, mkx
34741821668518216685 thlu_emf(k) = thlu(k)
3475 qtu_emf(k) = qtu(k)
3476 uu_emf(k) = uu(k)
3477 vu_emf(k) = vu(k)
347810383510451038351045 do m = 1, ncnst
3479 tru_emf(k,m) = tru(k,m) !<-Water tracers handled here
3480 enddo
3481 !*************
3482 !water tracers
3483 !*************
34841821668518216685 if(trace_water) then
34857286674091083425 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
3486 wtu_emf(k,m) = wtu(k,m) !Set initial values
3487 end do
3488 end if
3489 !*************
3490 end do
3491
34926530881240723 do k = kpen - 1, kbup, -1 ! Here, 'k' is an interface index at which
3493 ! penetrative entrainment fluxes are calculated.
3494
3495653088653088 rhos0j = ps0(k) / ( r * 0.5_r8 * ( thv0bot(k+1) + thv0top(k) ) * exns0(k) )
3496
3497 if( k .eq. kpen - 1 ) then
3498
3499 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3500 ! Note that 'ppen' has already been calculated in the above 'iter_scaleh' !
3501 ! loop assuming zero lateral entrainmentin the layer 'kpen'. !
3502 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3503
3504 ! -------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3505 ! Calculate returning mass flux, emf ( < 0 ) !
3506 ! Current penetrative entrainment rate with 'rpen~10' is too large and !
3507 ! future refinement is necessary including the definition of 'thl','qt'!
3508 ! of penetratively entrained air. Penetratively entrained airs across !
3509 ! the 'kpen-1' interface is assumed to have the properties of the base !
3510 ! interface of 'kpen' layer. Note that 'emf ~ - umf/ufrc = - w * rho'. !
3511 ! Thus, below limit sets an upper limit of |emf| to be ~ 10cm/s, which !
3512 ! is very loose constraint. Here, I used more restricted constraint on !
3513 ! the limit of emf, assuming 'emf' cannot exceed a net mass within the !
3514 ! layer above the interface. Similar to the case of warming and drying !
3515 ! due to cumulus updraft induced compensating subsidence, penetrative !
3516 ! entrainment induces compensating upwelling - in order to prevent !
3517 ! numerical instability in association with compensating upwelling, we !
3518 ! should similarily limit the amount of penetrative entrainment at the !
3519 ! interface by the amount of masses within the layer just above the !
3520 ! penetratively entraining interface. !
3521 ! -------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3522
3523587635661113 if( ( umf(k)*ppen*rei(kpen)*rpen ) .lt. -0.1_r8*rhos0j ) limit_emf(i) = 1._r8
3524587635627709 if( ( umf(k)*ppen*rei(kpen)*rpen ) .lt. -0.9_r8*dp0(kpen)/g/dt ) limit_emf(i) = 1._r8
3525
3526587635587635 emf(k) = max( max( umf(k)*ppen*rei(kpen)*rpen, -0.1_r8*rhos0j), -0.9_r8*dp0(kpen)/g/dt)
3527 thlu_emf(k) = thl0(kpen) + ssthl0(kpen) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kpen) )
3528 qtu_emf(k) = qt0(kpen) + ssqt0(kpen) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kpen) )
3529 uu_emf(k) = u0(kpen) + ssu0(kpen) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kpen) )
3530 vu_emf(k) = v0(kpen) + ssv0(kpen) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kpen) )
35313349519533495195 do m = 1, ncnst
3532 tru_emf(k,m) = tr0(kpen,m) + sstr0(kpen,m) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kpen) ) !<-Water tracers handled here.
3533 enddo
3534 !*************
3535 !water tracers
3536 !*************
3537587635587635 if(trace_water) then
353823505402938175 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
3539 wtu_emf(k,m) = wt0(kpen,m) + sswt0(kpen,m) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kpen) ) !Set initial values
3540 end do
3541 end if
3542 !*************
3543 else ! if(k.lt.kpen-1).
3544
3545 ! --------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3546 ! Note we are coming down from the higher interfaces to the lower interfaces. !
3547 ! Also note that 'emf < 0'. So, below operation is a summing not subtracting. !
3548 ! In order to ensure numerical stability, I imposed a modified correct limit !
3549 ! of '-0.9*dp0(k+1)/g/dt' on emf(k). !
3550 ! --------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3551
35526545365453 if( use_cumpenent ) then ! Original Cumulative Penetrative Entrainment
3553
35546545383515 if( ( emf(k+1)-umf(k)*dp0(k+1)*rei(k+1)*rpen ) .lt. -0.1_r8*rhos0j ) limit_emf(i) = 1
35556545378689 if( ( emf(k+1)-umf(k)*dp0(k+1)*rei(k+1)*rpen ) .lt. -0.9_r8*dp0(k+1)/g/dt ) limit_emf(i) = 1
35566545365453 emf(k) = max(max(emf(k+1)-umf(k)*dp0(k+1)*rei(k+1)*rpen, -0.1_r8*rhos0j), -0.9_r8*dp0(k+1)/g/dt )
3557 if( abs(emf(k)) .gt. abs(emf(k+1)) ) then
35586545265452 thlu_emf(k) = ( thlu_emf(k+1) * emf(k+1) + thl0(k+1) * ( emf(k) - emf(k+1) ) ) / emf(k)
3559 qtu_emf(k) = ( qtu_emf(k+1) * emf(k+1) + qt0(k+1) * ( emf(k) - emf(k+1) ) ) / emf(k)
3560 uu_emf(k) = ( uu_emf(k+1) * emf(k+1) + u0(k+1) * ( emf(k) - emf(k+1) ) ) / emf(k)
3561 vu_emf(k) = ( vu_emf(k+1) * emf(k+1) + v0(k+1) * ( emf(k) - emf(k+1) ) ) / emf(k)
356237307643730764 do m = 1, ncnst !<-Water tracers handled here.

35795757 do m = 1, ncnst

3598 thlu_emf(k) = thl0(k+1)

3600 uu_emf(k) = u0(k+1)
3601 vu_emf(k) = v0(k+1)

3618 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3619 ! In this GCM modeling framework, all what we should do is to calculate heat !
3620 ! and moisture fluxes at the given geometrically-fixed height interfaces - we !
3621 ! don't need to worry about movement of material height surface in association !
3622 ! with compensating subsidence or unwelling, in contrast to the bulk modeling. !
3623 ! In this geometrically fixed height coordinate system, heat and moisture flux !
3624 ! at the geometrically fixed height handle everything - a movement of material !
3625 ! surface is implicitly treated automatically. Note that in terms of turbulent !
3626 ! heat and moisture fluxes at model interfaces, both the cumulus updraft mass !
3627 ! flux and penetratively entraining mass flux play the same role -both of them !
3628 ! warms and dries the 'kbup' layer, cools and moistens the 'kpen' layer, and !
3629 ! cools and moistens any intervening layers between 'kbup' and 'kpen' layers. !
3630 ! It is important to note these identical roles on turbulent heat and moisture !
3631 ! fluxes of 'umf' and 'emf'. !
3632 ! When 'kbup' is a stratocumulus-topped PBL top interface, increase of 'rpen' !
3633 ! is likely to strongly diffuse stratocumulus top interface, resulting in the !
3634 ! reduction of cloud fraction. In this sense, the 'kbup' interface has a very !
3635 ! important meaning and role : across the 'kbup' interface, strong penetrative !
3636 ! entrainment occurs, thus any sharp gradient properties across that interface !
3637 ! are easily diffused through strong mass exchange. Thus, an initialization of !
3638 ! 'kbup' (and also 'kpen') should be done very cautiously as mentioned before. !
3639 ! In order to prevent this stron diffusion for the shallow cumulus convection !
3640 ! based at the Sc top, it seems to be good to initialize 'kbup = krel', rather !
3641 ! that 'kbup = krel-1'. !
3642 ! ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3643
3644 end do
3645
3646 !------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3647 ! !
3648 ! Compute turbulent heat, moisture, momentum flux at all interfaces !
3649 ! !
3650 !------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3651 ! It is very important to note that in calculating turbulent fluxes !
3652 ! below, we must not double count turbulent flux at any interefaces.!
3653 ! In the below, turbulent fluxes at the interfaces (interface index !
3654 ! k) are calculated by the following 4 blocks in consecutive order: !
3655 ! !
3656 ! (1) " 0 <= k <= kinv - 1 " : PBL fluxes. !
3657 ! From 'fluxbelowinv' using reconstructed PBL height. Currently,!
3658 ! the reconstructed PBLs are independently calculated for each !
3659 ! individual conservative scalar variables ( qt, thl, u, v ) in !
3660 ! each 'fluxbelowinv', instead of being uniquely calculated by !
3661 ! using thvl. Turbulent flux at the surface is assumed to be 0. !
3662 ! (2) " kinv <= k <= krel - 1 " : Non-buoyancy sorting fluxes !
3663 ! Assuming cumulus mass flux and cumulus updraft thermodynamic !
3664 ! properties (except u, v which are modified by the PGFc during !
3665 ! upward motion) are conserved during a updraft motion from the !
3666 ! PBL top interface to the release level. If these layers don't !
3667 ! exist (e,g, when 'krel = kinv'), then current routine do not !
3668 ! perform this routine automatically. So I don't need to modify !
3669 ! anything. !
3670 ! (3) " krel <= k <= kbup - 1 " : Buoyancy sorting fluxes !
3671 ! From laterally entraining-detraining buoyancy sorting plumes. !
3672 ! (4) " kbup <= k < kpen-1 " : Penetrative entrainment fluxes !
3673 ! From penetratively entraining plumes, !
3674 ! !
3675 ! In case of normal situation, turbulent interfaces in each groups !
3676 ! are mutually independent of each other. Thus double flux counting !
3677 ! or ambiguous flux counting requiring the choice among the above 4 !
3678 ! groups do not occur normally. However, in case that cumulus plume !
3679 ! could not completely overcome the buoyancy barrier just above the !
3680 ! PBL top interface and so 'kbup = krel' (.forcedCu=.true.) ( here, !
3681 ! it can be either 'kpen = krel' as the initialization, or ' kpen > !
3682 ! krel' if cumulus updraft just penetrated over the top of release !
3683 ! layer ). If this happens, we should be very careful in organizing !
3684 ! the sequence of the 4 calculation routines above - note that the !
3685 ! routine located at the later has the higher priority. Additional !
3686 ! feature I must consider is that when 'kbup = kinv - 1' (this is a !
3687 ! combined situation of 'kbup=krel-1' & 'krel = kinv' when I chose !
3688 ! 'kbup=krel-1' instead of current choice of 'kbup=krel'), a strong !
3689 ! penetrative entrainment fluxes exists at the PBL top interface, & !
3690 ! all of these fluxes are concentrated (deposited) within the layer !
3691 ! just below PBL top interface (i.e., 'kinv-1' layer). On the other !
3692 ! hand, in case of 'fluxbelowinv', only the compensating subsidence !
3693 ! effect is concentrated in the 'kinv-1' layer and 'pure' turbulent !
3694 ! heat and moisture fluxes ( 'pure' means the fluxes not associated !
3695 ! with compensating subsidence) are linearly distributed throughout !
3696 ! the whole PBL. Thus different choice of the above flux groups can !
3697 ! produce very different results. Output variable should be written !
3698 ! consistently to the choice of computation sequences. !
3699 ! When the case of 'kbup = krel(-1)' happens,another way to dealing !
3700 ! with this case is to simply ' exit ' the whole cumulus convection !
3701 ! calculation without performing any cumulus convection. We can !
3702 ! choose this approach by specifying a condition in the 'Filtering !
3703 ! of unreasonable cumulus adjustment' just after 'iter_scaleh'. But !
3704 ! this seems not to be a good choice (although this choice was used !
3705 ! previous code ), since it might arbitrary damped-out the shallow !
3706 ! cumulus convection over the continent land, where shallow cumulus !
3707 ! convection tends to be negatively buoyant. !
3708 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
3709
3710 ! --------------------------------------------------- !
3711 ! 1. PBL fluxes : 0 <= k <= kinv - 1 !
3712 ! All the information necessary to reconstruct PBL !
3713 ! height are passed to 'fluxbelowinv'. !
3714 ! --------------------------------------------------- !
3715
3716587635587635 xsrc = qtsrc
3717 xmean = qt0(kinv)
3718 xtop = qt0(kinv+1) + ssqt0(kinv+1) * ( ps0(kinv) - p0(kinv+1) )
3719 xbot = qt0(kinv-1) + ssqt0(kinv-1) * ( ps0(kinv-1) - p0(kinv-1) )
3720587635587635 call fluxbelowinv( cbmf, ps0(0:mkx), mkx, kinv, dt, xsrc, xmean, xtop, xbot, xflx )
372126500563825326 qtflx(0:kinv-1) = xflx(0:kinv-1)
3722
3723587635587635 xsrc = thlsrc
3724 xmean = thl0(kinv)
3725 xtop = thl0(kinv+1) + ssthl0(kinv+1) * ( ps0(kinv) - p0(kinv+1) )
3726 xbot = thl0(kinv-1) + ssthl0(kinv-1) * ( ps0(kinv-1) - p0(kinv-1) )
3727587635587635 call fluxbelowinv( cbmf, ps0(0:mkx), mkx, kinv, dt, xsrc, xmean, xtop, xbot, xflx )
372826500563825326 slflx(0:kinv-1) = cp * exns0(0:kinv-1) * xflx(0:kinv-1)
3729
3730587635587635 xsrc = usrc
3731 xmean = u0(kinv)
3732 xtop = u0(kinv+1) + ssu0(kinv+1) * ( ps0(kinv) - p0(kinv+1) )
3733 xbot = u0(kinv-1) + ssu0(kinv-1) * ( ps0(kinv-1) - p0(kinv-1) )
3734587635587635 call fluxbelowinv( cbmf, ps0(0:mkx), mkx, kinv, dt, xsrc, xmean, xtop, xbot, xflx )
373526500563825326 uflx(0:kinv-1) = xflx(0:kinv-1)
3736
3737587635587635 xsrc = vsrc
3738 xmean = v0(kinv)
3739 xtop = v0(kinv+1) + ssv0(kinv+1) * ( ps0(kinv) - p0(kinv+1) )
3740 xbot = v0(kinv-1) + ssv0(kinv-1) * ( ps0(kinv-1) - p0(kinv-1) )
3741587635587635 call fluxbelowinv( cbmf, ps0(0:mkx), mkx, kinv, dt, xsrc, xmean, xtop, xbot, xflx )
374226500563825326 vflx(0:kinv-1) = xflx(0:kinv-1)
3743
37443349519534082830 do m = 1, ncnst
37453349519533495195 xsrc = trsrc(m)
3746 xmean = tr0(kinv,m)
3747 xtop = tr0(kinv+1,m) + sstr0(kinv+1,m) * ( ps0(kinv) - p0(kinv+1) )
3748 xbot = tr0(kinv-1,m) + sstr0(kinv-1,m) * ( ps0(kinv-1) - p0(kinv-1) )
37493349519533495195 call fluxbelowinv( cbmf, ps0(0:mkx), mkx, kinv, dt, xsrc, xmean, xtop, xbot, xflx )
3750151053192218043582 trflx(0:kinv-1,m) = xflx(0:kinv-1)
3751 enddo
3752

3754 !water tracers
3755 !*************
3756587635587635 if(trace_water) then
375723505402938175 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
375823505402350540 xsrc = wtsrc(m)
3759 xmean = wt0(kinv,m)
3760 xtop = wt0(kinv+1,m) + sswt0(kinv+1,m) * ( ps0(kinv) - p0(kinv+1) )
3761 xbot = wt0(kinv-1,m) + sswt0(kinv-1,m) * ( ps0(kinv-1) - p0(kinv-1) )
376223505402350540 call fluxbelowinv( cbmf, ps0(0:mkx), mkx, kinv, dt, xsrc, xmean, xtop, xbot, xflx )
37631060022415301304 wtflx(0:kinv-1,m) = xflx(0:kinv-1)
3764 end do
3765 end if
3766 !*************
3767
3768 ! -------------------------------------------------------------- !
3769 ! 2. Non-buoyancy sorting fluxes : kinv <= k <= krel - 1 !
3770 ! Note that when 'krel = kinv', below block is never executed !
3771 ! as in a desirable, expected way ( but I must check if this !
3772 ! is the case ). The non-buoyancy sorting fluxes are computed !
3773 ! only when 'krel > kinv'. !
3774 ! -------------------------------------------------------------- !
3775
3776587635587635 uplus = 0._r8
3777 vplus = 0._r8
37784085140851 do k = kinv, krel - 1
37794085140851 kp1 = k + 1
3780 qtflx(k) = cbmf * ( qtsrc - ( qt0(kp1) + ssqt0(kp1) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
3781 slflx(k) = cbmf * ( thlsrc - ( thl0(kp1) + ssthl0(kp1) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) ) * cp * exns0(k)
3782 uplus = uplus + PGFc * ssu0(k) * ( ps0(k) - ps0(k-1) )
3783 vplus = vplus + PGFc * ssv0(k) * ( ps0(k) - ps0(k-1) )
3784 uflx(k) = cbmf * ( usrc + uplus - ( u0(kp1) + ssu0(kp1) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
3785 vflx(k) = cbmf * ( vsrc + vplus - ( v0(kp1) + ssv0(kp1) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
378623285072328507 do m = 1, ncnst
3787 trflx(k,m) = cbmf * ( trsrc(m) - ( tr0(kp1,m) + sstr0(kp1,m) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
3788 enddo

3790 !water tracers
3791 !*************
37924085140851 if(trace_water) then
3793163404204255 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
3794 wtflx(k,m) = cbmf * ( wtsrc(m) - ( wt0(kp1,m) + sswt0(kp1,m) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1))))
3795 end do
3796 end if

3800 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3801 ! 3. Buoyancy sorting fluxes : krel <= k <= kbup - 1 !
3802 ! In case that 'kbup = krel - 1 ' ( or even in case 'kbup = krel' ), !
3803 ! buoyancy sorting fluxes are not calculated, which is consistent, !
3804 ! desirable feature. !
3805 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
3806
380720914902679125 do k = krel, kbup - 1
380820914902091490 kp1 = k + 1
3809 slflx(k) = cp * exns0(k) * umf(k) * ( thlu(k) - ( thl0(kp1) + ssthl0(kp1) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
3810 qtflx(k) = umf(k) * ( qtu(k) - ( qt0(kp1) + ssqt0(kp1) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
3811 uflx(k) = umf(k) * ( uu(k) - ( u0(kp1) + ssu0(kp1) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
3812 vflx(k) = umf(k) * ( vu(k) - ( v0(kp1) + ssv0(kp1) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
3813119214930119214930 do m = 1, ncnst
3814 trflx(k,m) = umf(k) * ( tru(k,m) - ( tr0(kp1,m) + sstr0(kp1,m) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
3815 enddo
3816 !*************
3817 !water tracers
3818 !*************
381920914902091490 if(trace_water) then
3820836596010457450 do m=1,wtrc_nwset
3821 wtflx(k,m) = umf(k) * ( wtu(k,m) - ( wt0(kp1,m) + sswt0(kp1,m) * ( ps0(k) - p0(kp1) ) ) )
3822 end do
3823 end if
3824 !*************
3825 end do

3827 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
3828 ! 4. Penetrative entrainment fluxes : kbup <= k <= kpen - 1 !
3829 ! The only confliction that can happen is when 'kbup = kinv-1'. For this !
3830 ! case, turbulent flux at kinv-1 is calculated both from 'fluxbelowinv' !
3831 ! and here as penetrative entrainment fluxes. Since penetrative flux is !
3832 ! calculated later, flux at 'kinv - 1 ' will be that of penetrative flux.!
3833 ! However, turbulent flux calculated at 'kinv - 1' from penetrative entr.!
3834 ! is less attractable, since more reasonable turbulent flux at 'kinv-1' !
3835 ! should be obtained from 'fluxbelowinv', by considering re-constructed !
3836 ! inversion base height. This conflicting problem can be solved if we can!
3837 ! initialize 'kbup = krel', instead of kbup = krel - 1. This choice seems!
3838 ! to be more reasonable since it is not conflicted with 'fluxbelowinv' in!
3839 ! calculating fluxes at 'kinv - 1' ( for this case, flux at 'kinv-1' is !
3840 ! always from 'fluxbelowinv' ), and flux at 'krel-1' is calculated from !
3841 ! the non-buoyancy sorting flux without being competed with penetrative !
3842 ! entrainment fluxes. Even when we use normal cumulus flux instead of !
3843 ! penetrative entrainment fluxes at 'kbup <= k <= kpen-1' interfaces, !
3844 ! the initialization of kbup=krel perfectly works without any conceptual !
3845 ! confliction. Thus it seems to be much better to choose 'kbup = krel' !
3846 ! initialization of 'kbup', which is current choice. !
3847 ! Note that below formula uses conventional updraft cumulus fluxes for !
3848 ! shallow cumulus which did not overcome the first buoyancy barrier above!
3849 ! PBL top while uses penetrative entrainment fluxes for the other cases !
3850 ! 'kbup <= k <= kpen-1' interfaces. Depending on cases, however, I can !
3851 ! selelct different choice. !
3852 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !

3973 nlten_sub = 0._r8
3974 niten_sub = 0._r8

3982 qtten_sub = g * comsub(k) * ( qt0(k) - qt0(k-1) ) / ( p0(k-1) - p0(k) )
3983 qlten_sub = g * comsub(k) * ( ql0(k) - ql0(k-1) ) / ( p0(k-1) - p0(k) )

3985 nlten_sub = g * comsub(k) * ( tr0(k,ixnumliq) - tr0(k-1,ixnumliq) ) / ( p0(k-1) - p0(k) )

4051 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
4052 ! Tendencies of thermodynamic variables. !
4053 ! This part requires a careful treatment of bulk cloud microphysics.!
4054 ! Relocations of 'precipitable condensates' either into the surface !
4055 ! or into the tendency of 'krel' layer will be performed just after !
4056 ! finishing the below 'do-loop'. !
4057 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------- !
4058
4059587635587635 rliq = 0._r8
4060 rainflx = 0._r8

4066
4067 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
4068 ! Compute 'slten', 'qtten', 'qvten', 'qlten', 'qiten', and 'sten' !
4069 ! !
4070 ! Key assumptions made in this 'cumulus scheme' are : !
4071 ! 1. Cumulus updraft expels condensate into the environment at the top interface !
4072 ! of each layer. Note that in addition to this expel process ('source' term), !
4073 ! cumulus updraft can modify layer mean condensate through normal detrainment !
4074 ! forcing or compensating subsidence. !
4075 ! 2. Expelled water can be either 'sustaining' or 'precipitating' condensate. By !
4076 ! definition, 'suataining condensate' will remain in the layer where it was !
4077 ! formed, while 'precipitating condensate' will fall across the base of the !
4078 ! layer where it was formed. !
4079 ! 3. All precipitating condensates are assumed to fall into the release layer or !
4080 ! ground as soon as it was formed without being evaporated during the falling !
4081 ! process down to the desinated layer ( either release layer of surface ). !
4082 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
4083
4084 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
4085 ! 'dwten(k)','diten(k)' : Production rate of condensate within the layer k !
4086 ! [ kg/kg/s ] by the expels of condensate from cumulus updraft. !
4087 ! It is important to note that in terms of moisture tendency equation, this !
4088 ! is a 'source' term of enviromental 'qt'. More importantly, these source !
4089 ! are already counted in the turbulent heat and moisture fluxes we computed !
4090 ! until now, assuming all the expelled condensate remain in the layer where !
4091 ! it was formed. Thus, in calculation of 'qtten' and 'slten' below, we MUST !
4092 ! NOT add or subtract these terms explicitly in order not to double or miss !
4093 ! count, unless some expelled condensates fall down out of the layer. Note !
4094 ! this falling-down process ( i.e., precipitation process ) and associated !
4095 ! 'qtten' and 'slten' and production of surface precipitation flux will be !
4096 ! treated later in 'zm_conv_evap' in 'convect_shallow_tend' subroutine. !
4097 ! In below, we are converting expelled cloud condensate into correct unit. !
4098 ! I found that below use of '0.5 * (umf(k-1) + umf(k))' causes conservation !
4099 ! errors at some columns in global simulation. So, I returned to originals. !
4100 ! This will cause no precipitation flux at 'kpen' layer since umf(kpen)=0. !
4101 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
4102
4103 dwten(k) = dwten(k) * 0.5_r8 * ( umf(k-1) + umf(k) ) * g / dp0(k) ! [ kg/kg/s ]
4104 diten(k) = diten(k) * 0.5_r8 * ( umf(k-1) + umf(k) ) * g / dp0(k) ! [ kg/kg/s ]
4105
4106 ! dwten(k) = dwten(k) * umf(k) * g / dp0(k) ! [ kg/kg/s ]
4107 ! diten(k) = diten(k) * umf(k) * g / dp0(k) ! [ kg/kg/s ]
4108
4109 !*************
4110 !Water tracers:
4111 !*************
4112 if(trace_water) then
41132174194027177425 do m=1,wtrc_nwset !Loop over water species
4114 wtdwten(k,m) = wtdwten(k,m) * 0.5_r8 * ( umf(k-1) + umf(k) ) * g / dp0(k) ! [ kg/kg/s ]
4115 wtditen(k,m) = wtditen(k,m) * 0.5_r8 * ( umf(k-1) + umf(k) ) * g / dp0(k) ! [ kg/kg/s ]
4116 end do
4117 end if
4118 !*************
4119
4120 ! --------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
4121 ! 'qrten(k)','qsten(k)' : Production rate of rain and snow within the layer k !
4122 ! [ kg/kg/s ] by cumulus expels of condensates to the environment.!
4123 ! This will be falled-out of the layer where it was formed and will be dumped !
4124 ! dumped into the release layer assuming that there is no evaporative cooling !
4125 ! while precipitable condensate moves to the relaes level. This is reasonable !
4126 ! assumtion if cumulus is purely vertical and so the path along which precita !
4127 ! ble condensate falls is fully saturared. This 're-allocation' process of !
4128 ! precipitable condensate into the release layer is fully described in this !
4129 ! convection scheme. After that, the dumped water into the release layer will !
4130 ! falling down across the base of release layer ( or LCL, if exact treatment !
4131 ! is required ) and will be allowed to be evaporated in layers below release !
4132 ! layer, and finally non-zero surface precipitation flux will be calculated. !
4133 ! This latter process will be separately treated 'zm_conv_evap' routine. !
4134 ! --------------------------------------------------------------------------- !
4135
413654354855435485 qrten(k) = frc_rasn * dwten(k)
4137 qsten(k) = frc_rasn * diten(k)
4138
4139 !*************
4140 !Water tracers:
4141 !*************
4142 if(trace_water) then
41432174194027177425 do m=1,wtrc_nwset !<-loop over water species
4144 wtrpten(k,m) = frc_rasn*wtdwten(k,m)
4145 wtspten(k,m) = frc_rasn*wtditen(k,m)
4146 end do
4147 end if
4148 !*************
4149
4150 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------------- !
4151 ! 'rainflx','snowflx' : Cumulative rain and snow flux integrated from the !
4152 ! [ kg/m2/s ] release leyer to the 'kpen' layer. Note that even !
4153 ! though wtw(kpen) < 0 (and umf(kpen) = 0) at the top interface of 'kpen' !
4154 ! layer, 'dwten(kpen)' and diten(kpen) were calculated after calculating !
4155 ! explicit cloud top height. Thus below calculation of precipitation flux !
4156 ! is correct. Note that precipitating condensates are formed only in the !
4157 ! layers from 'krel' to 'kpen', including the two layers. !
4158 ! ----------------------------------------------------------------------- !
4159
416054354855435485 rainflx = rainflx + qrten(k) * dp0(k) / g
4161 snowflx = snowflx + qsten(k) * dp0(k) / g
4162
4163 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
4164 ! 'slten(k)','qtten(k)' !
4165 ! Note that 'slflx(k)' and 'qtflx(k)' we have calculated already included !
4166 ! all the contributions of (1) expels of condensate (dwten(k), diten(k)), !
4167 ! (2) mass detrainment ( delta * umf * ( qtu - qt ) ), & (3) compensating !
4168 ! subsidence ( M * dqt / dz ). Thus 'slflx(k)' and 'qtflx(k)' we computed !
4169 ! is a hybrid turbulent flux containing one part of 'source' term - expel !
4170 ! of condensate. In order to calculate 'slten' and 'qtten', we should add !
4171 ! additional 'source' term, if any. If the expelled condensate falls down !
4172 ! across the base of the layer, it will be another sink (negative source) !
4173 ! term. Note also that we included frictional heating terms in the below !
4174 ! calculation of 'slten'. !
4175 ! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ !
4176
4177 slten(k) = ( slflx(km1) - slflx(k) ) * g / dp0(k)
4178 if( k .eq. 1 ) then
4179587635587635 slten(k) = slten(k) - g / 4._r8 / dp0(k) * ( &
4180 uflx(k)*(uf(k+1) - uf(k) + u0(k+1) - u0(k)) + &
4181 vflx(k)*(vf(k+1) - vf(k) + v0(k+1) - v0(k)))
418248478509695700 elseif( k .ge. 2 .and. k .le. kpen-1 ) then
418342602154260215 slten(k) = slten(k) - g / 4._r8 / dp0(k) * ( &
4184 uflx(k)*(uf(k+1) - uf(k) + u0(k+1) - u0(k)) + &
4185 uflx(k-1)*(uf(k) - uf(k-1) + u0(k) - u0(k-1)) + &
4186 vflx(k)*(vf(k+1) - vf(k) + v0(k+1) - v0(k)) + &
4187 vflx(k-1)*(vf(k) - vf(k-1) + v0(k) - v0(k-1)))
4188587635587635 elseif( k .eq. kpen ) then
4189587635587635 slten(k) = slten(k) - g / 4._r8 / dp0(k) * ( &
4190 uflx(k-1)*(uf(k) - uf(k-1) + u0(k) - u0(k-1)) + &
4191 vflx(k-1)*(vf(k) - vf(k-1) + v0(k) - v0(k-1)))
4192 endif
419354354855435485 qtten(k) = ( qtflx(km1) - qtflx(k) ) * g / dp0(k)
4194
